patch.value: Install the pinned release npm into a job-local prefix

The release workflow replaces the runner's global npm with the pinned npm. Parallel jobs on one runner host share the toolcache Node installation, so one job's global install mutates a sibling job's npm mid-install (ENOTEMPTY, or npm: command not found), as reported by unbraind/pm-ops#284 for the fleet.

The release workflow installs the pinned npm with --prefix into a job-local directory and prepends that prefix bin to the job path; The workflow keeps the exact-version assertion on the effective npm; A workflow-contract test fails if any workflow replaces the global npm

1. Segment-scoped prefix exception: run scripts now split into command segments at unquoted ;, &, | and newlines. The scanner tracks quote state across lines and $( … ) substitutions (which nest a fresh quoting context even inside double quotes), skips comments and here-document bodies, and any script that cannot be delimited with confidence (unbalanced quote or substitution) fails closed as 'undelimitable command line'. The job-local prefix exception now only covers the segment carrying it; rejected fixtures add 'npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/npm-11.19.0" npm@11.19.0 && npm install -g npm@11.19.0' and 'npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/npm-local" npm@11.19.0; npm install -g npm@11.19.0'. 2. Combined short flags: any single-dash letter cluster containing g now marks global (rejected: 'npm install -gpld npm@11.19.0', 'npm install -dg npm@11.19.0'); 'npm install -D pnpm' and 'npm install -gpld pnpm' stay accepted.
3. Workflow, job and step env compose for each step run, the step scope taking precedence; npm reads npm_config_* keys case-insensitively. npm_config_global set to anything other than false/0/empty, npm_config_location=global, a ${{ … }} expression value, or an unreadable env scope makes every npm install in that run global unless its own segment carries a job-local prefix.
